**B.** Under the suspect's account, he never resisted the arrest. He struck the officer only to stop nightstick blows after the arrest was complete, which is self-defense against excessive force rather than the conduct the statute bans. Under the officer's account, he used force against a lawful arrest, which violates the statute, so the verdict turns on which account the jury believes. The shared note's claim that an unlawful arrest strips all privilege to use force conflicts with the common-law rule that reasonable force may be used against an unlawful arrest, so I don't rely on it.

CONFIDENCE: 60
